what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard the town manager's preliminary FY24 capital plan, which recommends six projects as top priorities out of the requests ranked.
Funding for the plan is a mix of tax revenue, unexpended capital and the special purpose stabilization fund, with free cash set aside for the overlay account.
Ten-year capital requests far exceed average spending, leaving a large unfunded amount; the town manager will re-evaluate the plan before town meeting to see if more can go to unfunded projects.
Members discussed lake-area assessment increases and what abatements could mean for the overlay account; no votes were taken on them.
The minutes of January 12 were approved and the meeting adjourned.

why_it_matters: The capital plan decides which town buildings and equipment get paid for from taxes and reserves, and the unfunded remainder is what town meeting voters will be asked to weigh.
Lake-area abatements are paid out of the overlay account, which draws on free cash, so a wave of abatements is a mechanism that could reduce money available for other uses.
